# Release model {#release-model}

Kailash versions by **release train and lock** — the lockfile is the
version of the system, and releases are named `YYYY.NN`
([the versioning record](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/blob/master/docs/spec.md#76-release-versioning--cadence--how-a-release-version-is-created)):

- **`YYYY.NN` release index** — `2026.01`, `2026.02` — where NN counts
  releases within the year, not the calendar month. A train may GA
  after the calendar page turns (`2026.02` may GA in January 2027) and
  keeps its name.
- **Staged ladder** — `2026.01-alpha.1` → `-rc.1` → bare `2026.01`
  (GA). Bare numbers are reserved for GA so a pre-GA cut is honest at
  tag-verification time; a material re-cut of a GA in its release
  month is `2026.01.1`.
- **Cut discipline** — every cut runs a standing checklist: lane
  residue swept off the train's target (leftovers re-scoped with a
  one-line reason, never silence), both repositories eval-clean across
  systems, manifest validation with the census snapshot in sync, VM/VM
  acceptance evidence recorded, a lock-bump release PR whose body is
  the release review, and a reference-hygiene pass over everything
  about to go public. The lock-bump PR lands **before** the signed
  tag; tag verification runs a real cache pull and the validator
  output goes into the release notes.

## Update automation behind a release

Between releases, machine-driven checks work their cadences (weekly
for fast-moving tool classes, monthly for the `nixpkgs` refresh) but
every outcome is a reviewed pull request — dependency automation
proposes, a human approves, smoke gates decide what is even proposed.
Nothing updates a user's system unprompted: an install moves forward
when its operator rebuilds against a newer lock or adopts a release.
